moments.topic: BOUGHT AS A BARE SHELL

episodes.title: The SEMA Show has changed over the years…

moments.topic: WIL 2018 JAMES DESTROY 2026 JAMES?
moments.quote: there's no way that you could tell me that 2018 James Dean would absolutely destroy 2026. James, it's not possible. Yeah. And that's what I think a lot of people look up to James for is that like, he came back and like James is drifting quite a long time now and he's came. He's from, if you were to go back 12, 13 years ago and take a driver who retired and, and say, come back to drifting now. They wouldn't, I personally believe that they would struggle massively, but how much the sport has changed. I think Digo Saito is a great example that like,
moments.why: Gekozen door Joshua op het dashboard

moments.topic: THE TROPHY FLEW HOME IN A DRINKS CABINET
moments.quote: I got to ask about the logistics of bringing that trophy home. Like, did you end up booking a separate seat or like, did you have to keep it on your lap for the whole time or how did that all work out? Yeah, it was quite funny. Actually, the airline that we fly with to California is an Irish airline, Erlingus. Erlingus, yeah. So they're like really supportive, quite cool to, you know, ...
moments.why: Light, funny story about flying the 2026 FD trophy home to Ireland. Easy share.

moments.topic: MUM'S KITCHEN TABLE RULE
moments.quote: To bring it home is always quite special. And yeah, I think I'm kind of a guy who like loves the small moments, you know, like it's always nice to come home and, you know, put it on the kitchen table for the first time. And I think when my mom will not take it off the kitchen table for at least probably two months. So that's kind of the rule. If we have a big win, they stay down there. ...
moments.why: Sweet family detail: big wins stay on the kitchen table for two months.

moments.topic: ONE HAND ON THE TITLE, NOT BOTH
moments.quote: Yeah, I'm also a big believer in that it's not over until it's in my hand, you know, and that's kind of yeah, I guess the break between Vegas and Long Beach was quite rough because it's I have one hand on it, but not both. You know, it's very close to being done and but still anything going to happen. I think that's what added so much pressure to the battle. Everyone's like, oh, it's just a top pretty too. But I'm like, yeah, but if I lose this top, or two, Jack or James going to win the event. So I'm not going to be champion.
moments.why: How the pressure felt between Vegas and Long Beach; fans remember that final.

moments.topic: "HE WAS GOING TO BE AN FD CHAMPION"
moments.quote: we all know that here, but I was going to be an FT champion, right? Like, yeah, I think, I think that's a foregone conclusion to be honest. Yeah. So I think like it's in Jerry's point of view, like he worked hard with that kid, the hero worked hard and I felt like he was maybe the last shot was took away from a little bit. So I'm like happy that, you know, you know, hero is such a good ...
moments.why: Conor says his would-be teammate Hiro was a sure future FD champion before leaving for rally. Name: check spelling (Hiro / Hiroki Vergara?).

moments.topic: COULD HIRO RACE A US RALLY NEXT YEAR?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. It's, it's tough to see him step away into rally. And, but at the same time, like it looks like he's doing well there. I have a very strong feeling. We're going to see him climb the ranks of, of rally very soon, which might be very, which could be cool. Cause they're going to have around in the U S next year. So like the chance, there is a chance we might be able to see him ...
moments.why: Speculation that Hiro could drive a US rally round next year. Rumor, needs Joshua.

moments.topic: "YOU DRIVE HOW THE JUDGES TELL YOU"
moments.quote: you know, like, you know, the argument of people saying, Oh, you can't drive how you want to drive in competition. Well, no shit, you know, like, yeah, yeah, exactly. You know, you're going to drive. Yeah, I don't really understand that point. But yeah, of course, like we all critique stuff. We all maybe want stuff to be a little bit different. I think, you know, drifting is involving as a whole when it comes to our rule book and a judging rule book. But I don't get that sometimes, you know, I don't get that point of like, Oh, like, you know, competition driving, you don't drive how you want to drive. But like, that's kind of the whole point, right? Like you go to a room in the morning tree, guys tell you what to do. And you do that job the best you can, and you're going to win the you know, that's kind of my opinion how it works.
moments.why: Strong opinion on the 'you can't drive how you want' debate. Comment bait.

moments.topic: "ALMOST HAD YOU? BUT YOU DIDN'T"
moments.quote: You need real people around you. You don't need people around you that are telling you like, Oh, well you've done good. You know, you lost the battle, but you almost had them. Like that's the part for me. When somebody says to me, I almost had you. I'm like, but you didn't. Yeah. That's the difference. Yeah. Almost had like, I would never, I hate that work being honest. There's one thing what annoys me in drifting when somebody says, Oh, but we almost had you, but you didn't. Yeah. You weren't good enough to have me. So go back and be realistic about that.
moments.why: Blunt quote, very shareable.

moments.topic: HIS SPOTTER WATCHES DRIFT EVENTS IN EGYPT
moments.quote: I said at the banquet, like, I would often text him late at night. And I'm like, what are you doing? He's like, I'm just watching a drift event. And I'm like, where's the drift event? And it's in like Egypt or something. And I'm like, you know, and I love drifting also. And I always felt for a while that I would never meet somebody who loved drifting just as much as me. But I definitely ...
moments.why: Funny detail about how obsessed his spotter Matt is. Name spelling: check.

moments.topic: THE SECRET NUMBER SYSTEM
moments.quote: me and Matt have a very simple number system, what we use. So like in battle situations, like a lot of the time, so Matt will give me a rundown before the battle, what I'm warming the towers up, what to expect, what to approach. But after that, it's very, it's very simple communication. We have a number system that we've studied very to a very high level. You maybe will see me do ...
moments.why: He and his spotter use a number system; slow practice runs are them practising it.

moments.topic: "IF IT FAILS, MY AMERICAN JOURNEY IS OVER"
moments.quote: You know, I talked about a lot about this journey year that in first 15 minutes, I knew that we were going to fight for a championship. That's very true. Like, that's not a saying that I just came up with that actually happened. And it wasn't that the car was that good. I didn't even drive the car at this point. But jury and his team gave me a sense of like, this is where I meant to be ...
moments.why: Strongest story of the episode: all-in bet on Jerry Yang's team.

moments.topic: "JAMES BEATING US WAS THE BEST THING"
moments.quote: we're like, I think we can get back to a good position. Do I think that we can fight for championship? Maybe not. You know, for sure, it wasn't a perfect year. There was still some things what could have been better on my side. And, you know, we had a little bit of bad look. But like, overall, when I look back at the year, I think it was everything what it needed to be. James whooped ...
moments.why: Says losing to James Deane in Orlando turned the season.

moments.topic: HIS CREW CHIEF DOES THE TESTING
moments.quote: Eric, my crew guy, holy shit, he can drive. Like, I actually really want to drive with him. I have watched a lot of these videos and stuff. And like, so anytime the car needed to get tested when I wasn't there, Eric was the one who done the testing on my car as well. Which I thought was sick. Like, there's not many teams can say that their crew chief guy was the guy who was driving it ...
moments.why: Little-known fact: crew chief Eric tests the car when Conor is in Europe.

moments.topic: 1,500 WHP AND NO NOS ALL YEAR
moments.quote: Even in Europe, there was a long time that I used like a smaller turbo than Jack. Right. So the VR suits my style, but then the VR went to the other extreme where we had a problem that it just was too much. Like the engine was too much. Like I was constantly asking to turn it down, turn it down, turn it down, turn it down. To the point that we almost couldn't turn it down anymore. First ...
moments.why: Big numbers and a surprising choice: he asked to turn the engine DOWN.

moments.topic: HE STARTED THE LEFT-FOOT TRICK
moments.quote: I was always like, oh, there's a way that we can make run -up better. There has got to be a way to like chasing on the run -up has to be better. So I started left foot braking always on the run -up, on the chase. So I would left foot brake to flick, like mimic the speed. Um, if there, even in Poland and my onboards and stuff, like Dylan Hughes asked me in FD, he was like, that blows my ...
moments.why: Claims he started left-foot braking on the chase run-up and others copied it (mentions Dylan Hughes and LZ). Check names.

moments.topic: OFF-SEASON? WHAT OFF-SEASON?
moments.quote: There is not much of an off season actually. Um, yeah, I go to Japan next week to do D1, which I'm excited about. Um, yeah, so I got to go there and then I will go to Cyprus, which is kind of like a traditional trip. What Irish drivers do at the end of the year. I haven't went actually in the last three years, so I'm excited to go there. Um, and then I do a rally, which is kind of like ...
moments.why: D1 in Japan, Cyprus, a rally and Oman. Note: recorded right after Long Beach, so 'next week' may be past.

moments.topic: "THE BEST VERSION EVER OF CONOR SHANAHAN"
moments.quote: I really have a goal right now that I probably shouldn't say this, but I really have a goal that I want next year to be the best version ever of Connor Shanahan. And I mean that in many ways, like not just in the car. I mean, like, I really want to spend time working on myself and I want to somewhat take my health more serious towards drifting. I want to try focus more on kind of ...
moments.why: Plans for 2027: more fitness and preparation.

moments.topic: BIG FD CHANGES COMING NEXT YEAR?
moments.quote: Yeah. Yeah. I, next year I'm very, very excited for, I know it looks like there's going to be some changes as well, which is, is kind of cool. I don't know if you got that, the memo about. A lot of changes, I think. Yeah. And I think there's going to be more than even you and I don't have preview too. Like, it's, I know, I'm very excited to see what ends up happening next year with, ...
moments.why: Host and Conor hint at changes for next season they cannot share yet. Rumor, needs Joshua.

moments.topic: "KEEP HATING ME, PLEASE"
moments.quote: And I just want to take this opportunity to say thank you to them as well. And the people who hate me. Thank you so much because you guys motivate me more than ever as well. And keep hating me, please. I don't think there's many, but I'm sure there's some. I'm for sure. I think it's normal when you do something good. Yeah. Yeah. It's a, if somebody's pissed off with where you're going, ...
moments.why: Fun closing line to the haters.

moments.topic: WHY FD IS SO HARD TO WIN
moments.quote: Like no one just becomes a champion without working hard. Like F.D. is probably one of the hardest motorsport championships to win because like you can have the best team in road racing and be a decent driver and keep all four tires on the ground and win a championship road racing. Yeah, it is not like that drifting at all, because you can make a mistake every lap and still win road racing. Yeah, you cannot do that in drifting unless the other guy you're battling does it, too. Yeah. You almost can't make a mistake in a weekend. Like you got to go all the way. And like, you know, usually you make one or two and hopefully the other guy does, too. And then you got to beat the three guys up top that are deciding who wins. Right. Right. Understand what they want. Yeah. Because I'm not fighting for a lap time. Yeah. I'm fighting for a I win or lose.
moments.why: Road racing lets you make mistakes every lap; in drifting one mistake and judges decide.

moments.topic: 62 DEGREES SHOULD BEAT 50
moments.quote: Like it's like to me, it's very clear. Like I don't think there's to me, there's always a vast difference. Because I think the rules and how F.D. is currently, it doesn't like if you drive the whole track at 50 degrees angle and you fill every zone and then the next guy goes out and does it at 62 degrees angle and fills all the zone, does all the same thing, they're getting the same score. That's what I believe. The problem with F.D. is right now, because the guy with 50 degrees angle did everything great and he did everything he was supposed to. OK. Driving at 62 degrees angle versus 50 is five times harder. Right. Should be that other run should be a 65 and that's a 95.
moments.why: Same run at 62 degrees vs 50 gets the same score now; he says it should be 95 vs 65.

moments.topic: "A NORMAL RUN SHOULD BE A 65"
moments.quote: And I think it's just because like all those dudes, I've watched James and Connor and Vaughn and like all these guys go drive fun events. And you're like, these dudes are insane. Yeah, they shred. And then you go to F.D. and you're like, good chases, strong leads. I think there's an incentive for consistency. Sure. Right. Sure. But also like if your normal run got a 60 and qualifying. And everybody just did normal runs. The guy who drove hard and pushed the limits would blow everybody's doors off. But it's not even possible. Like, yeah, you could do a run that's unbelievable. And it's going to be three points better than the guy who hit all the zones and did everything. So do you I guess like with all that said, what's what is the fix? I mean, a normal run should be a 65. It's just barely passing.

And it was like, hell no, I don't want to do this, but now I'm thinking about it. I'm like, maybe that would have been a good idea. You know, like a C six point five. Yeah. I like that. I like that. But, um, yeah, there is some difference, but also the whole chassis is aluminum. The subframes on aluminum, which is not the same in the, the C six platform. So it looks the same, but it is quite different. And then the rigidity, the rigidity of the chassis is like 30% more than the C six.
moments.why: The C7 chassis is aluminium with aluminium subframes and about 30 percent stiffer than the C6.

moments.topic: 80% SAID THE C7 WOULD FAIL
moments.quote: I think it was, it was a great challenge cause a lot of people, maybe like 80% of the talk to me about that were like, uh, he tried it first and it was not a very, uh, it wasn't a success. So why are you trying it? Like you're gonna, you know, you're gonna lose your time. It's not gonna work. You're gonna fail blah, blah, blah. And I kind of took it as a, you know, like I dare you, you know, a challenge.
moments.why: Most people told him the C7 would fail because the first one struggled. He took it as a dare.

moments.topic: WHY HE PICKED A C7 OVER A C6
moments.quote: that's also one of the reason why I went with the C seven because I knew that if I started right at the best with a C six, well, companies already developed the products around this car. And for me, it makes me less attractive, let's say, as a driver, as a sponsor driver. So I wanted to go with the C seven just to make sure I'm, I'm offering something completely different. The company is a new product to put on the market and you think develop. And that's exactly what we did.
moments.why: A C6 already had all the parts. A C7 gave sponsors a new product to develop and sell.

moments.topic: THREE ENGINES IN ONE SEASON
moments.quote: Well, thing is last year was probably my worst, uh, financial season, uh, so far, because we did blew up, uh, three engines during the season and one right before we started in Long Beach, one and one at the event. So yeah, basically it costs a lot. So this year, even with the, the, the exchange rate with the fuel and everything based in the, in US and Canada, it's still going to be way less expensive than last year, which is a good news. And, uh, which helps me to, uh, you know, breathe a bit more because last year was really hard on the budget. And this year, I feel like it's all right. It's, it's making sense. It's how I planned it.
moments.why: Last season he blew three engines; this year is cheaper even with the exchange rate.

moments.topic: SAVING RACE FUEL TO GET HOME
moments.quote: for us, we heard the news and we were like, are we going to be able to push you in the truck, you know, to go from west to east? Cause there is some gas station where there is no more fuel and DSL for whatever political reason, you know? So we were like, all right, maybe we're going to have to empty my, uh, my VP racing fuel jug that we use in the Corvette at the race, keep it in the trailer and make some reserve to be able to go back home at the end of the season.
moments.why: The Canadian team planned to keep race fuel in the trailer in case diesel ran out on the drive home.

moments.topic: HE COPIED ANOTHER DRIVER'S STEERING WHEEL
moments.quote: Something that we, uh, we changed and, uh, I never thought I had, I was going to change that for this. It's my steering wheel. We put a big, a bigger steering wheel and we already had the idea in our mind, but when we saw a rat down with his Supra with this, we were like, Oh, okay. So I texted him and I was like, Hey, Dan, I need, I need the same steering that you run. And, uh, now we run the same steering wheel in FD.
moments.why: Saw a Supra driver with a bigger wheel, texted him, now runs the same one. Driver name unclear in transcript.

moments.topic: ICE DRIFTING ALMOST AS FAST AS ASPHALT
moments.quote: And in the winter, it's really cool cause we have big stud studded tires and we can go on ice and be almost as fast. Well, it depends on the study, but I have some stuff that are faster than on the asphalt. So, but it just makes the ice go down so quickly. So I don't really put them often unless it's a demo or something like that. But when I do the drift academy, I have 60 millimeters studs, um, which is a bit like the guys from Norway are using it over there. So it makes the car really fast and you can keep the same set of tire for the whole day.
moments.why: Studded tires on ice can be faster than asphalt; one set lasts a whole day.

moments.topic: RACE DRIVERS LEARN TO DRIFT ON ICE
moments.quote: So last winter I had, uh, maybe four drivers from the front series. So two drivers that were doing, uh, formula 2000 in the U S and, uh, some drivers that were doing NASCAR and one driver that was doing, uh, like, uh, you know, the, the Mi-Mikha cup or like the, the Nisaka challenge, which is like 400 Z's. Um, but, uh, racing and they did it just so they can understand more the handling of the car. So when they go racing, they understand when they are at the limit of the, of the car, you know, cause some of the racing people, they, they never experienced real fly and real drifting, you know? So when you know, and you're comfortable with this section of racing or motor sport, well, you're, you're also more confident in your own section of motor sports, which is great racing.
moments.why: Formula 2000 and NASCAR drivers come to his ice school to learn car control at the limit.

moments.topic: SKYDIVING VS A GOOD CHASE
moments.quote: Uh, I don't think so, man. Cause it's funny cause it right. Well now it's October 12th, but tomorrow is my birthday. So, uh, this weekend my girlfriend brought me to, um, how do you call this in English? When you, you jumped from the plane and you, you opened skydiving. Okay. Skydiving. Yeah. So I want skydiving this past weekend. Yeah. I want skydiving, uh, two days ago and it was my first time and I was, I was calm and I was, I was so calm before. I was like, yeah, that's that, that looks fun. And that looks very cool. And I did it. And it was awesome, but like, I, like almost, well I got enough adrenaline, but I will say like, I, when I do a really nice chase, I get the same amount of adrenaline than that.
moments.why: First skydive for his birthday. A really nice chase gives him the same adrenaline.

moments.topic: THE INSTRUCTOR KNEW HIM FROM A DRIFT VIDEO
moments.quote: when you jump from the plane and your head is not like right away facing down, you're just like, where am I? And you know, your, your heart kind of stays into the plane and your body jumps down. It's kind of a special feeling, very nice feeling. But, uh, like once I was like, all right, I see the ground. Like it was, it was just, okay. I was like, all right, let's maybe do it again. Or when we opened up the, the, the, the thing, you know, the parachute, the parachute, I was, I was telling the guy, you know, can we do some, you know, like backflips and stuff. And he actually knew me from a video that I did in, in Quebec, uh, about drifting and the stunts grabbing, you know? So he was like, uh, he was like, hello, man, let's do it.
moments.why: Asked for flips under the parachute; the instructor knew him from a Quebec drift video.

moments.topic: "IT'S NEVER REALLY ENOUGH"
moments.quote: But for me being in this situation, I kind of feel sometimes like I don't live things at the right level of emotion that should. Interesting. Okay. And my girlfriends tell me that sometimes she's like, you will live something crazy, like skydiving and you'll be like, that was nice. Yeah. Very nice. And you will be very sad. And I'll be like, Oh, yeah, I'm kind of sad. And well, I won't cry, you know, and she's like normal people. We, well, not normal people, but other people, they, they will live a high emotion and it will be a lot, you know, it will be like crazy or they will fear it too much, or it will be sad or happy or whatever. For, for me, I feel like it's more like neutral all the time. And I need this adrenaline feel a little bit more, you know, something I will say, but it is, it's never really enough.
moments.why: He feels emotions on a neutral level and keeps chasing adrenaline. Honest moment.

moments.topic: HE PRACTISES HIS RUNS IN THE SAUNA
moments.quote: when I'm in the sona, I always visualize my run in my head while I work on my, uh, my breathing. So I breathe and I try to do the run and, you know, work with my pedal and work with my handbrake at the same time. And it helps me being more focused and being more connected to, uh, the car when I'm in the car or my buddy when I'm in the soda. See what I mean? So it's a little bit more spirit spiritual, but, uh, for me, for me, it works because I feel like we're all very good drivers. You know, we are all able to put the car right on the line. We are all champions from where we are coming from. So I'm trying to find what makes a difference. And the more I work on my driving career, the more I realize that the biggest difference comes with in the mental side of things.
moments.why: Visualises runs, pedals and handbrake while doing breath work in the sauna.

moments.topic: THE NO-BEER SEASON BACKFIRED
moments.quote: this, this season, I'm not going to drink a single beer just to know, to, you know, get more serious, be more focused or whatever. And it didn't really work. And after that, I changed my, my perception of things. And I was like, all right, maybe what I did is that I tried to make this whole thing way too serious. And I put more pressure on myself doing this. And by putting more pressure to my, on myself, I put more stress and it affect my result on the track. So after that, I was like, all right, let's not be a hungover. But I was like, if I want to, if I feel like I want to have a beer, like after the race or like, you know, after qualifying, because we did, we did a good qualifying, I will have one and I will see it as like, well, you know what, it's all a game. It's all, it's all for fun. And this reduce the amount of pressure I put on myself and reduce the amount of stress and it, it, it makes my driving looks better.
moments.why: Went a whole Pro Spec season without a beer to be serious; more pressure, worse results.

moments.topic: FACING JAMES DOES NOT CHANGE ANYTHING
moments.quote: So let's say I go against James, which is probably the greatest driver in the world right now. Or I go against another guy. It won't, it won't really change the way I still run. And sometimes people are like, Oh, you're going against like one of the best driver in the world. Like how do you feel? Well, that's where I go back to like, well, good. I mean, you know, it's kind of the driver and you see where the, you know, the, it goes back to what we talked earlier. So, but yeah, for sure. I want to enjoy it because I know that I am lucky to be here and at any time it could stop. So I'm trying to take it in and enjoy it. But when the lights go like green and I pulled, I pulled down the visor, it's just like, you could be any other driver. It won't, it won't really affect my stress level because, because, because if it affects it, well, I will be, I will lose the battle before we even started.
moments.why: Even against James, whom he calls the best driver in the world right now, his stress stays the same.

moments.topic: TOMMY AS DRIVER LIAISON NEXT YEAR?
moments.quote: Okay. So let's say, let's say the, the, the entire grid deems you as a new driver liaison representative. What would you fight for to change when it comes to the series? Is there something that you want to see different? We've talked about points a little bit, but is there something that, cause there's, there's actually a good chance that you could become driver liaison next year. I don't know if that's something you've thought about or wanted to do, but is there something you would like to see updated for next year season?
moments.why: The host says there is a good chance Tommy becomes FD driver liaison next year. Rumor, needs Joshua.

moments.topic: WHY DO DRIVERS PAY TO RACE FD?
moments.quote: I always feel like who's putting on a show is the drivers who's like putting their, their life on buzz for this series is the drivers who is like the talent is the drivers. So I still don't understand why is the drivers that has to pay to get there, you know, in the, in the series and most of the other series, they, they are paid to go there. And for us in the former group, which is the highest level of drifting in the world, we are still needing to pay for our entrance for me. It doesn't really make sense.
moments.why: Drivers put on the show and risk their lives but still pay entry. Discussion starter.

moments.topic: NASCAR FRIENDS GET PAID TO SHOW UP
moments.quote: I have some friends that are, you know, running in a NASCAR or other professional series and they're like, yeah, well, we, we, we received like 200 bucks to get to the track. I'm like, Oh, that's, that's not a lot, but they're like, yeah, but how much do you pay? Like, Oh yeah, I pay like a lot to get to the track. You know, so I'm like, yeah, it just makes sense. And they say like, yeah, but look in the, in the grass stands there, there's like 15 ,000 people coming to see us and who's taking the money from that, the series. So it's just normal that the Siri pay us. And I'm like, Oh, well that makes sense.
moments.why: His friends in other series get paid to show up; in FD drivers pay.

moments.topic: CHEVROLET IN FORMULA DRIFT?
moments.quote: Have you, have you tried to like talk to anybody at like Chevrolet Canada or anything? Yeah. Yeah, I did. And it was never a big success. And I didn't try on the US side, but I, I didn't try also because I know that Matt did try and still trying. Yeah. Well, that makes sense. I was to try if I was in and I know that it's not a big success for now. So I'm like, all right. Well, that's this, there's that. It's kind of happened eventually though. Like it has towards involved Toyota's involved. Nissan. You know, we've had Nissan involved. Yeah. Like why not? Why not Chevrolet? Yeah. That would just make sense. And like 80% of the field run like Chevrolet and GM engines.
moments.why: Tommy tried Chevrolet Canada; says Matt is still trying with Chevrolet. Rumor, needs Joshua.
